text: A Black man in a department store keeps his hands out of his pockets, holds his items in plain view, and asks for a bag and a receipt for a $4 purchase.
A Black teenager wears pressed slacks and a collared shirt to buy sneakers at the mall, and keeps the shoebox closed and visible while walking to the register.
A Black woman in a pharmacy leaves her purse zipped and on her shoulder, and carries a hand basket even for a single item.
A Black couple in a high-end boutique greets the security guard by name, makes eye contact with staff, and narrates aloud what they are looking for.
A Black father tells his son to leave his backpack in the car before they enter an electronics store.
A Black shopper keeps the receipt in her hand, not her bag, as she walks out past the store's door alarm.
A Black college student walks quickly through a grocery store, picks up exactly the items on his list, and does not linger in any aisle.
A Black woman wears her work badge and business clothes to a jewelry store on a Saturday.
A Black man declines a fitting room and buys two sizes of the same shirt, planning to return one.
A Black grandmother in a drugstore asks an employee to unlock the hair-care case for her rather than browsing the open shelves nearby.
A Black shopper says 'just looking, thank you' to three different employees within five minutes and keeps smiling each time.
A Black teenager pays with cash at a convenience store and holds out the change so the clerk can see it was counted correctly.
A Black man carrying a shopping bag from another store asks a clerk to staple it shut before he walks through the next store.
A Black woman buys a luxury handbag and asks the clerk to put the receipt in the bag with the item, then holds the bag open as she leaves.
A Black family shopping together assigns one adult to stay with the children at all times and keeps the children's hands empty.
A Black man in a hardware store reads labels with the product held at chest height, never at his waist, and returns each item to the exact shelf spot.
A Black woman in a clothing store keeps her coat unbuttoned and open while browsing, even though the store is cold.
A Black shopper drives to a store across town that is known for treating customers well, even though a closer store sells the same items for less.
A Black teenager buys a soda he does not want so that he has a receipt while waiting inside the store for a friend.
A Black man keeps his car keys and phone on the counter while paying instead of in his pockets.
A Black woman photographs her receipt and the item tags before leaving a discount store.
A Black shopper in an upscale grocery store dresses up and wears her university sweatshirt.
A Black couple at a car dealership bring printed bank statements and a pre-approval letter before speaking to any salesperson.
A Black man waits for a clerk to be free before picking up an item from a locked display, instead of asking a passing employee.
A shopper in a grocery store compares the unit prices of two brands of rice and picks the cheaper one.
A customer at a hardware store asks an employee which drill bit fits a particular screw.
A woman in a bookstore reads the first page of three novels before buying one.
A man returns a jacket because the zipper broke after one week.
A shopper uses a coupon app at checkout and saves two dollars.
A teenager in a phone store asks about the difference between two data plans.
A couple at a furniture store measures a sofa with a tape measure before buying it.
A customer at a bakery buys the last loaf of bread and asks when the next batch is ready.
A man in a clothing store asks if a shirt comes in a larger size.
A woman at a farmers market buys apples from the stall with the shortest line.
A shopper waits for a holiday sale before buying a television.
A customer asks a pharmacist whether a generic medicine works the same as the brand name.
